title: A Pet Fish Sells for a Reported $300,000, and Owners Buy It Eye Lifts

scenes.text: This fish has a Ferrari price and a plastic surgeon.
The Asian arowana, the dragon fish. Three feet long, armoured in big scales, and believed to bring luck and wealth.
One can sell for 150,000 dollars. A Malaysian breeder reportedly sold an albino for 300,000.
Owners pay for cosmetic surgery: 90 dollars for an eye lift, 60 for a chin job.
It's been stolen in waves. Four thefts in one week in Singapore, and a shop owner was killed over his stock.
In the United States you can't own one at all. It's protected under the Endangered Species Act. A Ferrari with fins.

description:
The Asian arowana, or dragon fish, is the world's most expensive aquarium fish: specimens sell for $150,000 and one albino reportedly fetched $300,000.
Owners pay for eye lifts and chin jobs for their fish, thefts and even a murder have been linked to the trade, and the species is banned in the United States under the Endangered Species Act.
Would you pay a house price for a fish?
subject: asian arowana
first_comment: There are stories of arowana leaping out of their tanks to warn owners of bad luck. Would you believe your fish?
